subtasks.text_content:
Book: pages 9 to 69. Introduction, plus Chapter 1: Essential Operating Principles.

Workbook: Chapter 1 section, plus pages ~80 to 85. Two pulls, not one.

Covers: setting your metronome, the core frameworks, build self-awareness to build mutual awareness, say the thing you think you cannot say, management vs leadership, come back to your operating system.

The workbook material this session needs:
Chapter 1: Management Prerequisites Checklist, Understand Your Values (adapted from Stan Slap), work style grid (introvert/extrovert against people/task oriented, producing Analyzer, Director, Collaborator, Promoter), strengths inventory split into innate vs acquired skills and capabilities.
Chapter 3, around pp. 80 to 85: "Working with Claire," her own worked example, and the "Working with Me" template. She files these as onboarding artifacts, not self-awareness ones. Pull them forward. The Chapter 1 exercises are the input, the Chapter 3 template is the container.

Sŏn output (draft):
Founder operating principles
Working-with-me document, Brandon
Working-with-me document, Dominic
Working-with-me template for the incoming chef partner, built as a prompt for that person, not filled in on their behalf

Notes: This feeds the operating agreement work already done with Dominic, and it is a direct input to the chef partner relationship. Chapter 1 is about the manager's self-awareness before it is about anyone else's.

Watch the Management Prerequisites Checklist. It assumes 1:1s, job ladders, levels, and a compensation philosophy. Sŏn has none of those yet and its compensation is embedded revenue share. Read it as a gap list, not a scorecard.

Completed 2026-09-11 (rerun)

Deliverable: page 2ky45bmy-31653 in the Sŏn Operating System doc. Eight sections: the six founder operating principles, the metronome, management and leadership, come back to your operating system, the prerequisites read as a gap list, the working-with-me document, the working-with-me template in full, and five instrument specifications. Thirty-three marks: nineteen recommended, ten founder-gated, three chef-gated, two team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

On the working-with-me outputs. The brief named filled documents for Brandon and Dominic. Those were not written, because the team does not generate a founder's interiority and the first pass was un-made partly for reaching there. What the session produced instead, on Brandon's instruction, is the complete template content: one spine of eleven prompts, each with what it asks, what it is really asking for, how to answer well, and what a weak answer looks like, plus three seat-specific preambles and three prerequisite self-exercises. Each founder completes their own. The chef partner's preamble is written as a prompt to that person and nothing is filled in on their behalf. The formatted fillable artifact is gated on the document methodology 86ajgn2z5 and is filed separately.

Filed: twelve typed work items under 86akh1hdg (six founder decisions, four documents, one instrument, one structure). Five carryovers in the register, linked to S2, S3, S4, S8, and S16.

Left open on purpose: when the working-with-me document is exchanged with the chef partner, which routes to S7 (86ajgnj8t). The first pass closed this without standing and the closure was un-made. This session did not close it either.

Two conflicts found inside the record itself, not between the book and Sŏn: the white paper and the brand canon disagree about who owns culinary identity (86akh2qnt), and they name the room-owning role differently (86akh2r3e). Both surfaced only because the white paper was read in full.

subtasks.text_content:
Book pages 70 to 83. Chapter 2, Founding documents. Workbook pp. 11 to 22: Stripe's Operating Principles as a worked example, and the Team Charter template.

Who supplies what, this session

This is a heavily-Brandon session. Read carryover 86ajgnpef before anything else. It governs.

Sŏn's mission, vision, and operating principles are decisions Brandon makes. They are not a synthesis of existing brand language, however elegant that synthesis would be.

The trap, named. Sŏn has a large body of stated material: brand canon (sources/brand-guidelines.md and sources/brand-guidelines-deck.pdf, held locally), the playground philosophy, code-bearing not load-bearing, and the three Korean frameworks. A Claude in this session can assemble a completely plausible Sŏn mission out of those fragments and write it down as settled. That is the failure. Brand canon is an input. It is not a substitute for the decision.

What Claude does here: structure the question. Show what a founding document has to do and what it breaks if it is wrong. Surface every place Sŏn already has an implicit answer and make the implicit explicit so Brandon can accept or reject it deliberately. Argue. Push. Refuse to let a phrase that sounds good pass as a decision.

What Claude does not do: write Sŏn's mission and mark it draft.

Propose freely. Record nothing as decided that Brandon has not said.

Sŏn output

The Sŏn operating charter, specification and structure, with every decision either supplied by Brandon in-session or logged as open. Instrument production is gated on 86ajgn2z5.

The distinction that must hold

Brand canon governs how Sŏn speaks, looks, and positions. The operating charter governs how the company runs, decides, and holds itself accountable. Two artifacts, two jobs. Do not let the charter drift into brand language. Do not let it contradict canon.

Inherited from S1, non-negotiable reads

Sŏn does not scale to 7,000 (86ajgnh8n). Her founding documents are written for a company that will inflate around them. Sŏn opens near full size and stays there. A charter written to organize growth is the wrong charter.

Founder job descriptions do not exist, for either founder. S1 identified this as an input to the operating agreement and the boundary that keeps a CEO and a CFO/CTO from quietly both owning the same thing until it breaks. It belongs in this session.

Compensation philosophy does not exist. S1 called it the largest live gap: Sŏn has a structure, not a philosophy. Decide here whether the philosophy belongs in the charter or waits for S13.

Filed by the Session 1 rerun, 2026-09-11

The record holds two accounts of the chef seat (86akh2qnt), with a founder decision at 86akh2qrp. The founder decision-rights rule does not exist (86akh2qt2), with a founder decision at 86akh2qht.

Two source corrections. Brand canon is the local files, not the archived ClickUp doc. The three profiles in profiles/ predate the allowlist; until 86akh2r4k lands, a session loading a profile applies the override in the context ledger.

Completed 2026-09-11

Deliverable: page 2ky45bmy-31673 in the Sŏn Operating System doc. Thirteen sections: what she asks for, the reframe for a house that does not inflate, the standing problem between canon and charter, the authority hierarchy conflict, the operating charter specification section by section, mission and long-term commitments and principles structured as decisions, the founding seat descriptions, founder decision rights, the chef seat, compensation philosophy, team charters, instrument specifications, and open questions routed. Thirty-three marks: eighteen recommended, twelve founder-gated, two chef-gated, one team-filled. Nothing landed, nothing final.

On the founding documents themselves. No mission, no long-term commitment, and no principle was written. Each was structured: what the instrument has to do, what makes one wrong, every candidate the record already holds quoted and tested against her own criteria, and exactly what Brandon supplies. Where a candidate reading was available it was named as a candidate, its source quoted, and what accepting it would commit Sŏn to stated. None was recorded as a draft. The canon's nearest mission-shaped sentence was tested and fails her uniqueness test.

Three conflicts found inside the record itself.

Canon claims authority the charter would contradict. The deck's cover reads "the source of truth for every decision made under this name"; the canon preamble says the tier hierarchy "governs all decisions." Both hold a rule for canon against a habit and canon against itself. Neither holds a rule for canon against another founding document. The clean split this brief assumed is not one canon agrees to.
The two canon artifacts state different six-tier hierarchies. brand-guidelines.md is Version 1.0; the deck is Version 3.0. The deck ranks the company non-negotiables at tier 2 with override authority over positioning, architecture, and every executional system, and adds "the order is the decision." The text version does not rank them at all. For a charter this decides whether "no disposable people" outranks a brand or service decision. Filed at 86akh3rx4 and 86akh3t00.
The chef seat conflict is about standing, not only ownership. The white paper's "chef partner" is an equal founding partner with a vote on whether a service period is built. Canon's "Executive Chef" is a hire gated by criteria the brand sets. A hiring criterion cannot be applied to a founding partner on the same terms. Extends 86akh2qrp at 86akh3tw9.

Two findings that reframed existing carryovers. The record assigns decision rights at least eight times without ever stating the rule, and the eight share one shape: closest competent owner, pre-stated range, escalation triggers named before the event. That pattern is recommended as the rule; the deadlock case stays founder-gated, sharpened with the interim two-partner case at 86akh3ty7. And the founder job descriptions have a concrete overlap already in the record: Brandon owns "the operating systems," Dominic owns "the technology build" and "the data architecture," and nobody owns the OS surface. Filed at 86akh3t27.

Resolved by the team. The compensation split: founding commitments in the charter because every hiring session needs them to score against, architecture in S13. Team charters: Sŏn deliberately does not use them at her unit, and uses a daypart charter instead, which is also the form the lunch decision takes.

Filed: eighteen typed work items under 86akh1hdg (eight founder decisions, three documents, two processes, two structures, three instruments, all three gated on 86ajgn2z5). Twelve carryovers in the register, linked to S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S12, S13, S16, and S17.

Left open, not closed here. Who carries the concept's voice to the team internally (86akh2qq0). The brief routed it to S2 and S2 did not close it. It now sits against the founding seat description work, since the record makes Brandon "the public voice" without saying who carries the voice inward.

Two record-integrity problems flagged. Both canon artifacts name the archived, excluded ClickUp doc 2ky45bmy-15773 as their record of truth, and the text canon says the Surface-and-Zone Baseline Document lives there, so a canon-referenced governing document is unreachable (86akh3tp5). The white paper names Airtable as its data-layer hub, and Airtable is no longer in use. Both feed the recommended charter design rule: commitments and owners, never tools or addresses.

A correction to this brief. It attributed "life share, not market share" and "the building is not the asset, the customer is" to the record. Neither is verbatim in the white paper. The record's claim is "The restaurant is the proof of concept. The connective layer is the asset" (WP p.34). Brand facts are not asserted from memory, and that applies to briefs as well as to output.

Sŏn output (draft): planning architecture and decision rights. Who decides what, on what information, at what altitude.

The hard part: her operating system is written for a hierarchical knowledge-work org. Brandon's stated organizational thesis is code-bearing, not load-bearing: the system asks what it knows and how that knowledge moves, rather than who holds authority over whom. These are not the same model. This session either reconciles them or names the departure explicitly. Do not paper over the difference.

Completed 2026-09-11

The hard part, answered rather than papered over. Section 3 names her five structural assumptions (a company-division-team-individual cascade; goals replicating down it; a manager above each person who assigns, reviews, and escalates; a leadership team allocating between internal claimants; communications pushed down a hierarchy), tests each against the record's web, and places all forty-seven of her mechanisms in one of three categories: survives intact, survives with its justification replaced, or does not survive. The departure is stated in one sentence: at Sŏn the unit that holds the information sets the goal, holds the metric, and owns the decision inside a pre-stated range; the center integrates and names the commitments; nothing is assigned, reviewed, or escalated by a person standing above another person. Two caveats are kept honest on the page: Sŏn is not self-managed, since authority is real and located in the domain, and what is absent is altitude rather than authority; and the web is a claim about a building that has not opened, which is what section 12 exists to test.

Decision rights, built from Sŏn's own record rather than imported. The rule in three parts: closest competent owner, range stated in advance, escalation triggers named before the event with a destination. Three operating rules attach: a trigger names its destination and "escalate" is not one; a range states what the owner may not do as well as what they may; ranges are set one level out from the position that holds them. The record's eight existing instances are quoted and rewritten into the form, five of them marked incomplete on a named part. Five classes the register does not yet cover are named with rules: decisions reserved to all partners, cross-domain consequence, lead-to-lead disagreement, emergency and closure, and stack changes. The interim two-partner case is argued to the founder ceiling and marked founder-gated.

The readiness test. Twenty yes-or-no rows, each with a check method and a named checker, replacing the retired prerequisites checklist. Run before dinner opens and at every phase gate; failures map to the record's five failure modes. Session 4 writes the cadence rows and completes the table.

Four conflicts found inside the record itself, the largest count of any session so far, and three are load-bearing.

The stack's data hub. The white paper (p.21) names a specific tool as "the hub for everything that is not CRM" and describes the AI layer as reading across it; the program's source boundary says that tool is out of use. The metric layer, the shift close, the feedback loop, the alert register, and readiness row 15 all run on whatever holds the role. Named, not resolved; the stack is Dominic's domain. Filed at 86akh5u6e.
Three service periods or four. Both canon versions state four dayparts and specify lunch fully with nothing marked held, and canon's own header rule makes every unmarked decision closed. The white paper states a core of three, with lunch "not assumed" and removable by a three-partner decision that cannot yet be taken. On status that is a disagreement, not an altitude difference; brunch is a second, smaller one, absent from canon entirely. The operating system resolves its own dependency by running whatever set of periods holds a ratified daypart charter, so the count is a parameter. Filed at 86akh5ubn.
Who owns the room. The white paper frees the Maitre d from the host stand to hold the floor; canon 1.0 gives the room to "the floor manager" and lists no Maitre d among uniform roles; the deck 3.0 lists both as distinct roles. This leaves the server's escalation destination, the transition trigger, and emergency authority with no seat to name. Filed at 86akh5u9g, routed to S8.
Further canon drift beyond the hierarchy: materiality, dinner lighting levels by zone, uniform roles, and token governance at the primitive tier. Added to Session 2's reconciliation item.

Stated candidly. The content framework's approval shares and her fixed-ratio horizon split are carried without their numbers, per the no-percentage rule. The financial half of strategic planning is a stated gap throughout. The leadership-line count and load for the requisite-variety test are a stated gap: the test is specified and its eight disturbance classes are named, but it cannot be run without the line list, which S8 produces. Two decision-rights values, the server's generosity range in value and the financial recovery threshold, are left as gaps and routed to S13 with Dominic's domain. The "naming" instance in the decision-rights carryover turned out to be token naming only; role naming, the loyalty layer, and future concepts have no entry and are marked as such.

Filed: thirty-five typed work items under 86akh1hdg (fourteen founder decisions, four documents, five processes, nine instruments, three structure; every instrument gated on 86ajgn2z5). Fifteen carryovers in the register, linked to S4 through S17. Every session from S4 onward now carries at least one; S9, S11, and S15 carried none after Session 2 and each carry one now.

A process note for later sessions. Subagent ClickUp access proved unreliable and inconsistent: of three subagents given ClickUp work, one succeeded and two reported an authorization they could not complete. Every task, link, and ledger write here was done by the session itself. The doc page was written by a subagent that made and self-corrected an omission partway through, so it was verified independently by fetching the page back and diffing it against the local source with shell tools rather than trusting the report. ClickUp's markdown serializer rewrites styling on read-back; normalize before comparing.
